evidence.claim: The uploaded source is a Blender 2.77 .blend file with SHA-256 ce670c397e3acad64c29a5b6498df3bd578f418a99b971f38c1d6634e6c0051b and size 6,290,220 bytes.
The player character is a gargoyle whose core interaction was punch, punch, counter.
The game was infinite, highly minimalist, and remembered as one of the most fun / best games Drew had made at the time or ever.
This was one of Drew's early characters where punch-based combat replaced his earlier sword-first instinct.

lessons.mechanism: A tiny combat verb set may sustain an infinite game when each input produces a strong state change and counterplay matters more than move-count variety.
lessons.evidence: USER_MEMORY only until source and gameplay evidence are inspected.
lessons.consequence: Test minimalist punch/counter loops as first-class combat designs instead of assuming content breadth is required for longevity.

lineage.relationship: Possible early punch/counter design lineage preceding later Gravity Fist combat work.

summary.strongestLesson: Minimal verb count may increase rather than reduce expressive game feel when the verbs sharply change tactical state.
